description:
From a childhood dream shaped by borders to documenting the most remote places on Earth in Antarctica and the Arctic, Esther Horvath takes us into the polar night of the northernmost community and the fastest‑warming place on the planet. There, she reveals the people who live far from their loved ones to understand and research our changing world, and the truths hidden behind the data. 

Esther Horvath is a documentary photographer dedicated to the polar regions, a National Geographic Explorer, and a photographer at the Alfred Wegener Institute Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research. She documents polar scientific expeditions and collaborates with scientists across a wide range of polar research fields. To date, she has taken part in 28 Arctic and Antarctic expeditions. We are all running on the track of success, often speeding up to keep pace with others until we stumble and forget to listen to our own hearts and bodies. When exhaustion comes, sometimes all we need is to pause and listen inward again.

Grow at a pace that feels right for you. Wellness is not about luxury or society’s expectations—it’s about doing what feels natural, what you want to return to. Wellness is a life you enjoy and choose to design for yourself.

In The Butterfly Effect of Small Acts of Love, Atlas Lad,  a North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics student, with a passion for the intersection of business, medicine, and innovative system design, traces how quiet moments on his grandfather’s porch sparked a lifelong question: how can we better cherish the people we love while they’re still here? That question inspired Embrace, a platform that sends heartfelt video montages to individuals facing serious health challenges. Drawing on personal experiences, time spent in hospitals, and emerging research, Atlas illustrates how simple gestures, a short video, a kind message, and a shared memory can uplift patients, strengthen families, and positively influence care teams. His talk ultimately challenges the audience to begin their own “butterfly effect” of compassion by reaching out to someone they love in a small, intentional way today.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk presents a new, low-cost approach to surgical navigation for deep brain lesions. Instead of relying on complex and expensive commercial navigation systems, the method uses freely available software—3D Slicer—combined with a pen-like mouse equipped with a gyroscope, allowing surgeons to navigate directly on the patient’s brain.

This technique makes it possible to reach deep-seated brain tumors that are not visible on the brain’s surface, offering an accessible alternative to traditional navigation systems that are often costly and difficult to implement. By simplifying navigation without compromising precision, the approach opens new possibilities for neurosurgical care, particularly in resource-limited settings.

The talk highlights how rethinking existing tools can lead to practical innovations that expand access, reduce costs, and improve outcomes in brain surgery. Dr. Moneer K. Faraj is an Iraqi neurosurgeon and Assistant Professor at the College of Medicine, University
title: Can Brain Tumors Be Navigated Without Expensive Technology? | Dr. Moneer K. Faraj | TEDxBaghdad

Saliha Büşra Selman Adıyaman

“Aynı zor koşullarda büyüyen çocukların hepsi aynı değildir.”

Saliha Büşra Selman Adıyaman’ın konuşması, görünmeyeni görünür kılan bir farkındalık sunuyor. Peki, aynı şartlarda büyüyen çocukları birbirinden ayıran şey nedir? Onun cevabı net: rutinler.

Gündelik hayatın kimsenin alkışlamadığı tekrarları; yani küçük, sıradan ama tutarlı alışkanlıklar… Hayat zorlaştığında, bu küçük rutinlerin fırtınayı sakinleştiren bir liman gibi çalıştığını söylüyor.

Perdenin çoğu zaman gösterişli olana açıldığını; ama asıl perdenin, sıradanlığın tekrarında saklı olduğunu hatırlatıyor. Çünkü perde arkasında mükemmellik değil, tutarlılık vardır. Rutin, evin görünmeyen terapisti gibi çalışır.

Mesajı net:
Küçük alışkanlıkları hafife alma. Kimsenin alkışlamadığı rutinler, en güçlü koruyucu faktörlerden biridir. Saliha B. Selman, Wisconsin-Madison Üniversitesi’nde İnsan Gelişimi ve Aile Çalışmaları alanında doktora yapmıştır. Araştırmalarında, erken çocukluk gelişiminde rol

In this heartfelt TEDx talk, Vineet Gupta, a marathoner and endurance athlete, shares how running helped him rebuild his life—physically, mentally, and emotionally. After facing a serious accident, weight gain, and personal rejection, he realized the real challenge wasn’t his career or background, but his lifestyle and lack of direction.

What began as a small decision to focus on fitness slowly turned into a disciplined habit. Through consistent effort, better routines, and support from the running community, Vineet transformed not just his health, but his mindset and self-belief.

This talk is not about speed or medals. It is about patience, consistency, and the power of showing up every day. It’s a reminder that even slow progress is progress—and that the journey itself can change who you become.

With 8 billion humans on Earth, rising chronic diseases, and accelerating climate change, one question becomes urgent: are our lifestyles silently destroying both our health and the planet?

In this eye-opening TEDx talk, Dr. Mahendra Narayan Kabra, Chief of Lifeline Computerized Clinic & Research Institute and a globally respected homeopath, presents a bold yet practical roadmap to reverse this crisis. Drawing from decades of medical practice and ecological insight, he explains how excessive consumption, fossil fuel dependence, and processed diets are at the root of chronic illness and environmental collapse.

Dr. Kabra introduces the idea of “constructive exercise”—productive physical activity like kitchen gardening and tree planting that heals the body while restoring the Earth. Priya, Global Transformation Leader and holder of a Doctorate in AI & Machine Learning, shares her deeply personal journey of leadership, motherhood, and technology. Dr. Priya reflects on moments where empathy was missing, systems lacked humanity, and yet ambition refused to pause. These experiences reshaped her leadership philosophy—one rooted in empathy, flexibility, and responsibility. She challenges the notion that women must choose between growth and caregiving, or ambition and authenticity.

In this powerful and deeply reflective TEDx talk, Dr. Saleha Ahmad, Communication and Purpose Coach, shares a life-shaping framework she calls the GPS to Success and Happiness. Rooted in her own journey through loss, resilience, and professional reinvention, this talk explores why many people achieve outward success yet struggle with inner fulfillment.

At a young age, Dr. Saleha faced personal tragedy that forced her to confront difficult questions about independence, purpose, and self-worth. Through these experiences—and years of coaching leaders—she discovered that lasting success depends on alignment. Alignment between what you want (Goals), who you truly are (Person), and how you structure your life and work (Systems).

description: This talk paints the picture of DeAnna's experience growing up with her sister, who happens to have Down syndrome. After a jolting doctor’s message at her sister’s birth, her mother decides to take her child home in 1973 and raise her with the same standards and expectations of her other children. It was a joyful and enriching childhood until her life took a dramatic turn at age 22 when she was mandated out of the public special education system. DeAnna realizes that her sister's experience is not unique but rather the overwhelming majority of every family’s experience with their loved one at age 22 who cannot access the services and support of a traditional .edu higher education degree. DeAnna and her co-founder Dr. Pamala Lindsay go on to create a higher educational model for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) which patterns itself after a traditional college based on the choice and interest of the student. title: Amplifying Silent Voices: A Higher Education Revolution | DeAnna Pursai | TEDxViikki

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk explores a deeply human journey that begins with migration but does not end at borders, where home travels in memory rather than in suitcases. Drawing from lived experience and artistic practice, Qais Al-Sindy examines how stereotypes are formed, how fear is produced, and how art can quietly dissolve both.

By transforming loss, pain, and displacement into shared spaces of reflection, the talk invites the audience to move from passive observation to active participation. It shows how trauma can become action, and grief can become a message, when expressed through an honest and human language.

Ultimately, the talk argues that art is not a wall but a bridge—one that connects cultures, reshapes perception, and opens a genuine path toward understanding and the possibility of peace. title: Breaking Stereotypes Through Art: When Beauty Becomes a Bridge | Qais Al-Sindy | TEDxBaghdad

Former advisor to Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Google DeepMind warns that AI isn't arriving in a vacuum - it's crashing into a world already facing climate breakdown, economic collapse, and democratic fragility. After 15 years advising some of the world's most influential leaders from Elon Musk to Mark Zuckerberg, and most recently leading global communications for Google DeepMind, Dex Hunter-Torricke walked away in October 2025.
